chunks: In this matter, victory or defeat is not dependent on the smallness or greatness of forces. It is Allah’s religion which He has raised above all faiths, and His army which He has mobilised and extended, till it has reached the point where it stands now, and has arrived its present positions. We hold a promise from Allah, and He will fulfil His promise and support His army.

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter/affair (referring to the Islamic cause or leadership)

ai.seo_question: What is the basis of victory in Islam according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this context, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) counters the conventional military reliance on troop numbers by emphasizing that the victory of Islam is divinely ordained and sustained by God's aid (tawfiq). This statement underscores the Shia theological principle that the 'army' of God is not merely physical but spiritual, affirming that divine promise (wa'd) is inevitably fulfilled regardless of worldly circumstances. It serves as a reminder that true strength lies in adherence to the divine covenant rather than material accumulation.
